questions.q: What does this lesson recommend as the basis for a performance tuning decision on the capstone project?
options: Evidence from Query History/Query Profile (e.g. partitions scanned, queueing) rather than applying every optimization out of habit
Applying every possible Chapter 10 technique regardless of whether it's needed
Guessing which table is probably slow
Skipping performance tuning entirely since it's optional
questions.explain: The lesson stresses one real, justified decision backed by evidence you actually looked at — high partitions scanned points to clustering, queueing points to warehouse sizing.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when does DirectQuery make more sense than Import for the capstone's Power BI connection?
options: When the Streams/Tasks pipeline keeps the data changing fast enough that Import's refresh lag would show stale numbers
Whenever the reporting tables are small, regardless of freshness needs
DirectQuery is always the better choice in every scenario
Only when Snowflake compute is free
questions.explain: DirectQuery trades per-query Snowflake compute cost for fresher data — worth it specifically when the underlying pipeline updates fast enough that Import's refresh lag would matter.

questions.q: What is the recommended order for presenting the capstone project, according to this lesson?
options: Layering and dimensional model, then TASK_HISTORY and SHOW GRANTS as proof, then the performance evidence and decision, then the Power BI report
Show the Power BI report first and nothing else
Read the raw landing tables' contents row by row
There is no recommended order — present however feels natural
questions.explain: The lesson lays out a specific walkthrough order that builds from foundational layering up to the connected report, each step proving a specific claim with real evidence.

questions.q: How should you demonstrate that the RBAC boundary on the analyst role is real, when presenting this project?
options: Run SHOW GRANTS on the analyst role live, rather than just stating that it was configured correctly
Show a screenshot of the GRANT statement being typed
Explain it verbally with no supporting evidence
Skip RBAC entirely during the presentation
questions.explain: The lesson repeatedly emphasizes proving claims with SHOW GRANTS output rather than asserting the RBAC setup is correct without evidence.

questions.q: According to this final lesson, what course does the Analytics Engineer career path move to next, and what does it build on from this capstone?
options: dbt — it takes the hand-built transformation layer (staging, star schema, MERGE logic) and shows how a real dbt project organizes, tests, and version-controls that same work
A second, unrelated Snowflake course covering the exact same material again
A course on Oracle Financial Applications
There is no next course — the Analytics Engineer path ends here
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly names dbt as the next course for the Analytics Engineer path, building directly on the transformation work done by hand in this capstone.
